<h1>Octave tree</h1>

The octave tree view lets you set the base octave per row of a given sequencer.
It also allows the design of per-row octave patterns that evolve in eight 4-step
chunks over a 2-bar cycle. So each row on a sequencer can have a **base octave**
different to the other rows and an additional **8-slot octave sequence** that
shifts the row's pitch up or down during playback.

---

## Per-row octave setting

An 8×8 grid, one row per sequencer row. **Column 4 is the centre marker** (a
mustard-coloured line down the grid) and represents an unmodified row. Pushing
buttons to the right of this will increase the octave, showing green for each
additional +ve octave modifier, and the same can be done to push a row to a
lower octave by pushing to the left of the centre, showing a red-lit button for
each additional -ve octave modifier.

So a row with three green cells sits three octaves up, and a row with two red
cells sits two octaves down. It can go up to +4, and down to -3 (three columns
to the left of centre, four to the right).

| Cells lit | Meaning | Colour |
|---|---|---|
| Column 4 only | Row plays at its normal octave | Mustard centre marker |
| Columns 5–8 | +1 … +4 octaves | Green |
| Columns 1–3 | −3 … −1 octaves | Red |

---

## Per-row octave sequencing

The octave a row plays at is the sum of the sequencer octave set overall for the
sequencer (hold SHIFT and use that sequencer's two LC buttons, the top one to
raise and the bottom one to lower), the base per-row octave you set on the left
pad as per the section above, and then the sequenced per-row octave, which is
the relevant per-row octave modifier for the given step that a sequencer is
playing.

The octave sequence is eight slots long and each slot covers four steps of the
bar, so it takes two bars to work through all eight:

| Bar | Steps 1–4 | Steps 5–8 | Steps 9–12 | Steps 13–16 |
|------|-----------|-----------|------------|-------------|
| Even | RHS slot 1 | RHS slot 2 | RHS slot 3 | RHS slot 4 |
| Odd | RHS slot 5 | RHS slot 6 | RHS slot 7 | RHS slot 8 |

So the sequence has two halves. Even bars use the first four slots and odd bars
the second four, giving an octave pattern that moves within the bar and shifts
again on alternating bars.

The per row octave setting is the left hand side, and the octave sequencing
is the right hand side of this image.

*The C minor chord from [Trigs](/documentation/MSEQ/trigs) pulled apart: the root row dropped an
octave to C2, the third stayed where it is, and the fifth lifted two octaves to
G5. The fill counts the base-octave shift, and the label on the outermost cell is
the note that row will now play. The meta-sequencer on the right adds movement:
the root row alternates +1 and +2 through its first four slots, while the G3 row
drops by 2 in slot 4 and by 1 in slot 8.*

On the right-hand pad each row is one sequencer row, and each of its eight cells
is one slot. Press a slot and its value cycles round. The colour tells you where
it landed, warm for down and green for up:

| Offset | Colour |
|---|---|
| −4 | <span style="display:inline-block;inline-size:.95em;block-size:.95em;background:#e31824;border:solid 1px rgba(219,219,219,0.5);vertical-align:-.12em;margin-inline-end:.55em"></span>Red |
| −3 | <span style="display:inline-block;inline-size:.95em;block-size:.95em;background:#b50e19;border:solid 1px rgba(219,219,219,0.5);vertical-align:-.12em;margin-inline-end:.55em"></span>Dark red |
| −2 | <span style="display:inline-block;inline-size:.95em;block-size:.95em;background:#c36705;border:solid 1px rgba(219,219,219,0.5);vertical-align:-.12em;margin-inline-end:.55em"></span>Burnt orange |
| −1 | <span style="display:inline-block;inline-size:.95em;block-size:.95em;background:#dde272;border:solid 1px rgba(219,219,219,0.5);vertical-align:-.12em;margin-inline-end:.55em"></span>Pale yellow |
| 0 | <span style="display:inline-block;inline-size:.95em;block-size:.95em;background:#000000;border:solid 1px rgba(219,219,219,0.5);vertical-align:-.12em;margin-inline-end:.55em"></span>Unlit |
| +1 | <span style="display:inline-block;inline-size:.95em;block-size:.95em;background:#b9f88c;border:solid 1px rgba(219,219,219,0.5);vertical-align:-.12em;margin-inline-end:.55em"></span>Pale green |
| +2 | <span style="display:inline-block;inline-size:.95em;block-size:.95em;background:#3a7a07;border:solid 1px rgba(219,219,219,0.5);vertical-align:-.12em;margin-inline-end:.55em"></span>Olive green |
| +3 | <span style="display:inline-block;inline-size:.95em;block-size:.95em;background:#007a0d;border:solid 1px rgba(219,219,219,0.5);vertical-align:-.12em;margin-inline-end:.55em"></span>Green |
| +4 | <span style="display:inline-block;inline-size:.95em;block-size:.95em;background:#2bff5e;border:solid 1px rgba(219,219,219,0.5);vertical-align:-.12em;margin-inline-end:.55em"></span>Bright green |

A slot at 0 is unlit, so a row with no movement in it stays dark and anything
lit is a shift.

Pressing a slot on its own walks through the whole range, which means passing
through values you don't want on the way. Hold an LC modifier to narrow it:

| LC modifier | Pressing a slot cycles it through |
|---|---|
| *(none)* | the full range, −4 … +4 |
| **SHIFT** | up only, 0 … +4 |
| **MUTE** | down only, −4 … 0 |
| **REC ARM** | resets that slot to 0 |

So SHIFT + MUTE are how you get to a value without walking past it, and REC
ARM is the quickest way to punch a single slot back out of the pattern.

The two pads add up. If the LP LHS puts a row at −3 and the first slot on the
LP RHS is +1, that row plays at −3 for most of the bar but lifts to −2 for
steps 1–4 of every even bar. Any slot can take any value, so you can be
constantly shifting, or shifting in an A/B style pattern over the two bars.

---

## Reset and Randomise

| Gesture | Effect |
|---------|--------|
| **SHIFT + MUTE**, press row R | Reset row R's base octave to 0 and all 8 sequence values to 0 (flat, no octave movement) |
| **SHIFT + SOLO**, press row R | Randomise: base octave → random in [−3, 4]; each sequence slot → random in [−4, 4] |
